{{nihongo|'''Tsumakirishima Shrine'''|東霧島神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Hyūga Province]].

'''Higashikirishima Shrine''' (つまきりしまじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Higashikirishima}} (つまぎりしま), {{ill|Miyakonojō|Q638301|qid=Q638301}}, {{ill|Miyazaki Prefecture|Q130300|qid=Q130300}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|Q135022904|qid=Q135022904}} for an {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Engishiki shrine|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and its former rank was prefectural shrine.

=== Overview ===
It is enshrined north of Miyakonojō, northwest of JR {{ill|Higashi Takasaki Station|id|Stasiun Higashi Takasaki|ja|東高崎駅|ko|히가시타카사키역|my|ဟိဂရှိတခဆခိဘူတာ|zh|東高崎站|qid=Q8190158}}.

It is said to have been founded in the reign of the 5th emperor, {{ill|Emperor Kōshō|Q312841|qid=Q312841}}. The shrine buildings were burned and buried in eruptions and fell into ruin, but in {{ill|Ōwa|de|Ōwa (Ära)|fa|اووا|fr|Ère Ōwa|ia|Owa (era)|id|Ōwa|ja|応和|ko|오와|ru|Ова (нэнго)|simple|Ōwa|sr|Ова|tr|Ōwa|uk|Ова|zh|應和|zh_yue|應和|qid=Q1324768}} 3 ({{ill|963|ab|963|af|963|am|963 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|963|ar|963|ary|963|arz|963|ast|963|avk|963|az|963|azb|۹۶۳ (میلادی)|bar|963|bcl|963|be|963|be_x_old|963|bg|963|bn|৯৬৩|bpy|মারি ৯৬৩|br|963|bs|963.|ca|963|cdo|963 nièng|ceb|963|ckb|٩٦٣|crh|963|cs|963|csb|963|cv|963|cy|963|da|963|de|963|el|963|eml|963|eo|963|es|963|et|963|eu|963|fa|۹۶۳ (میلادی)|fi|963|fo|963|fr|963|fy|963|ga|963|gan|963年|gd|963|gl|963|he|963|hi|९६३|hr|963.|ht|963 (almanak jilyen)|hu|963|hy|963|id|963|ilo|963|io|963|is|963|it|963|ja|963年|jv|963|ka|963|kaa|963|kk|963 жыл|ko|963년|la|963|lb|963|li|963|lij|963|lmo|963|lt|963 m.|lv|963. gads|map_bms|963|mdf|963|mg|963|mhr|963|mi|963|mk|963|mr|इ.स. ९६३|mrj|963 и|ms|963|mzn|۹۶۳|nah|963|nap|963|nds|963|new|सन् ९६३|nl|963|nn|963|no|963|nrm|963|nso|963|oc|963|or|୯୬୩|os|963-æм аз|pl|963|pnb|963|pt|963|qu|963|ro|963|ru|963 год|rue|963|sa|९६३|scn|963|sd|963ع|se|963|sh|963.|shn|963|si|963|simple|963|sk|963|sl|963|smn|963|sq|963|sr|963|su|963|sv|963|sw|963|tg|Соли 963|th|พ.ศ. 1506|tk|963|tl|963|tly|963|tr|963|tt|963 ел|uk|963|ur|963ء|uz|963|vec|963|vi|963|vls|963|war|963|wuu|963年|xmf|963|zh|963年|zh_min_nan|963 nî|zh_yue|963年|qid=Q23562}}), the Tendai monk {{ill|Shōkū|ja|性空|qid=Q11491623}} restored the shrine buildings, and in the Edo period it came to be called Higashikirishima Daigongen-gū<ref name="city">[https://www.city.miyakonojo.miyazaki.jp/site/kanko/10670.html 東霧島神社] - Miyakonojō City</ref><ref name="kanko-pre">[https://www.kanko-miyazaki.jp/spot/1022 東霧島神社] - Miyazaki Prefecture Tourism Association</ref>.

=== Enshrined deity ===
* {{ill|Izanagi|lt=Izanagi-no-Mikoto|qid=Q813858}}

=== Precincts ===
* Oniiwa steps - said to have been built in one night by an ogre stacking 999 stones; also called the “Do Not Look Back Slope,” where wishes come true if one chants with full focus and reaches the top without turning around<ref name="kanko-pre"/>.
* Shinseki (sacred stone) - said to be hardened tears of Izanagi-no-Mikoto after losing {{ill|Izanami|lt=Izanami-no-Mikoto|qid=Q682306}}, and its back has a sharp three-tiered cross section said to have been cut by Izanagi with a ten-hand sword (also a shrine treasure)<ref name="kanko-pre"/>.
